groups.title: Tailwind CSS Fundamentals
groups.question: You are styling your Next.js app with Tailwind and need a responsive layout and a dark mode toggle. Explain how Tailwind handles these.

followUps.Utility-first CSS and the Tailwind menta: What is the idea behind utility-first CSS?
followUps.Dark mode with Tailwind class strategy: How does the class strategy for dark mode work?

evidence.text: Styles are built from small single-purpose classes in the markup.
This removes the need to invent class names.
Styles live next to the markup they affect, so dead CSS is rare.
Unprefixed classes apply at all sizes.
Prefixes like md: apply from that width upward.
Responsive behaviour is visible directly in the class list.
Dark mode is on when a dark class is on the html element.
dark: classes apply only then.
Code can toggle the class for a user-controlled theme.

notEnough: Only saying you add dark: classes.

groups.title: Accessible Component Design
groups.question: Your UI looks slightly different on every page and screen reader users struggle with your custom components. Explain how you would build accessible, consistent components.

followUps.Semantic HTML and ARIA patterns for acce: Why use semantic HTML before ARIA?
followUps.Design tokens and consistent spacing sca: How do design tokens and a spacing scale keep the UI consistent?

evidence.text: Semantic elements carry roles and keyboard behaviour that assistive tools understand.
ARIA adds meaning only where HTML cannot express it.
Building accessibility in from the start is easier than fixing it later.
A fixed spacing scale stops arbitrary values.
Brand colors and sizes defined once in the config are reused everywhere.
Using the same tokens everywhere keeps screens consistent.

groups.title: shadcn/ui Component Library
groups.question: You are adding a component library with buttons in several sizes, a confirm dialog and toast messages. Explain how shadcn/ui works and how you would build variants.

followUps.Installing and using shadcn/ui component: How is shadcn/ui different from a normal component library?
followUps.Building reusable UI with variant patter: How does cva help define component variants?
followUps.Dialogs, toasts, and sheet components fo: When would you use a dialog, a toast or a sheet?

evidence.text: shadcn/ui copies component code into your project.
Components are built on accessible Radix primitives and styled with Tailwind.
You own the code and can change it, without waiting on a library update.

notEnough: Only saying it is a component library.

evidence.text: cva declares variants like size and intent as a map to classes.
Components expose a small, clear set of variant props.
The same variants are used everywhere, keeping the design consistent.
A dialog asks for a decision and blocks the page until answered.
A toast gives brief feedback without interrupting.
A sheet slides in from the side for secondary content or forms.

groups.title: Loading and Skeleton States
groups.question: Pages show blank areas while loading and conditional classes sometimes conflict. Explain how skeletons and the cn helper help.

followUps.Skeleton screens for perceived performan: Why show a skeleton instead of a spinner or a blank area?
followUps.cn utility for conditional Tailwind clas: What does the cn helper do?

evidence.text: A skeleton mimics the layout of the content that is coming.
It makes the wait feel shorter and prevents layout jumps.
Skeletons are used as Suspense fallbacks.
It joins class names conditionally.
tailwind-merge removes conflicting Tailwind classes, keeping the last one.
This lets callers safely override a component's default classes.
